Verdict: REVISE, with the main all-length construction acceptedThe neutral expansion theorem in    NEUTRAL_OCCUPIED_ENVELOPE_EXPANSION.md passes the mathematical audit under its stated freezing rule. The displayed matching is feasible and completely frozen for every  $m\ge2$  and every allowed  $S$ , including consecutive envelopes. The restricted budget and no-freezing lemmas are valid. The physical token cancellation is exact at the level of the specified  $(\text{tile},\text{index})$  identities.Two written points require correction:Section 1 must explicitly define  $g_m$ . Its current indexing clause stops at  $j<m$ , although  $g_mQ$  is subsequently used.Section 7 overstates the necessity of its particular cross matching. Complete freezing does require changing some original matching edges, but it does not require the specific edges  $C_ja_j,D_jd_j$ . Below I give an alternative all-length completely frozen matching on the same footprint that retains every original  $C_jD_j$ .The own-mate concern raised in the question is important, but it does not invalidate either supplied rank table: every listed nonselected witness has an actual mate of strictly smaller rank. No listed witness introduces the forbidden self-dependency.The conclusions below follow from symbolic coordinate, counting, and rank arguments. They do not rely on the finite verification reported in Section 8.1. The precise freezing rule and the own-mate issueLet  $\mu:P\to P$  be the fixed-point-free involution defined by the actual matching, and let  $N_R(x)$  denote the grid neighbours of  $x$  inside  $R$ . The intended dynamics should be written explicitly as
$$F_0=\varnothing,\qquad
F_{r+1}
=
F_r\cup
\left\{
x\in P:
\left|N_R(x)\cap\bigl(T\cup\mu(F_r)\bigr)\right|\ge2
\right\}.
\tag{5}$$
A valid rank certificate assigns a nonnegative integer  $\rho(x)$  to every endpoint and, for each  $x$ , supplies two distinct neighbouring sites  $y,z$ , each satisfying
$$y\in T
\quad\text{or}\quad
\bigl(y\in P\ \text{and}\ \rho(\mu(y))<\rho(x)\bigr),
\tag{6}$$
and similarly for  $z$ .This handles the circularity exactly. If a proposed witness were  $y=\mu(x)$ , then
$$\mu(y)=x,$$
so (6) would require  $\rho(x)<\rho(x)$ . Operationally, that witness becomes kept only after  $x$  itself has frozen and therefore cannot support its first freezing.Every witness in Sections 4–5 satisfies (6). Adding (5)–(6) would make the intended interpretation unambiguous, but the supplied strict tables already enforce it.The independent colour orders are also legitimate. A neighbour  $y$  has the opposite colour from  $x$ , while  $\mu(y)$  has the same colour as  $x$ . Thus every nonselected dependency remains within one colour. Rank induction proves that an endpoint of rank  $r$  freezes by round  $r+1$ .2. Footprint, matching, counts, and feasibilityThe terminal definition needs repairReplace the relevant clause of Section 1 by
$$g_j=(3,9+6j)\quad(0\le j\le m),\qquad
b_j=(3,10+6j)\quad(0\le j<m).
\tag{7}$$
Then  $g_m=(3,c)$ , so  $g_mQ$  is the intended terminal vertical edge. It would also be clearer to write  $0\le\ell<n$  explicitly for the lower endpoints.The original counts are correctThe matching edges are pairwise endpoint-disjoint, and
$$|M_0|
=
1+5(m+1)+m+1+n
=
9m+9.$$
The selection counts, by rows  $0,\ldots,5$ , are
$$3m+5,\quad 2m+3,\quad m+3,\quad 2,\quad 3,\quad 3m+5.$$
Consequently,
$$|T_0|=9m+21,\qquad
J_0=18m+30,\qquad
|R|=6(c+1)=36m+60.$$
The original feasibility assertion is valid. On rows  $0$  and  $5$ , every selection has empty horizontal neighbours and at most one possible occupied vertical neighbour. The interior selections are exhausted by the following table:Original selected siteIts occupied neighbour, if any $(1,2)$  $(1,1)$  $(1,4+6j)$  $A_j$  $(1,8+6j)$  $C_j$  $(2,0)$  $(2,1)$  $(2,3)$  $(3,3)$  $(2,9+6j)$  $g_j$  $(3,1)$  $(2,1)$  $(3,3)$  $(2,3)$  $(4,0),(4,2)$ None $(4,4)$  $Z_0$ This proves baseline feasibility uniformly in  $m$ .The expanded matching is validAt an expanded index, the six new endpoint sites comprise three original selections  $a_j,b'_j,f_j$  and three originally empty sites  $d_j,e_j,w_j$ . None is an original endpoint.Replacing  $C_jD_j$  by
$$C_ja_j,\qquad D_jd_j,\qquad w_jb'_j,\qquad f_je_j$$
matches those six new sites and the same two old endpoints exactly once. Every pair is a unit grid edge.For consecutive indices, the new rectangles occupy column intervals
$$[8+6j,10+6j],
\qquad
[14+6j,16+6j].$$
Their vertices and old attachment endpoints are disjoint. Therefore the construction is a matching for arbitrary  $S$ , and
$$\Delta |T|=-3s,\qquad
\Delta |M|=3s,\qquad
\Delta |P|=6s$$
are exact.Expanded feasibility has no hidden consecutive-envelope exceptionConverting a selection into an endpoint preserves occupancy at that site. Only  $d_j,e_j,w_j$  become newly occupied. Their neighbour sets are
$$\begin{aligned}
N_R(d_j)&=\{a_j,D_j,f_j,H_j\},\\
N_R(e_j)&=\{b'_j,f_j,U_{j+1},b_j\},\\
N_R(w_j)&=\{a_j,b'_j,f_j,(0,9+6j)\}.
\end{aligned}$$
After conversion, all neighbours in the first two lines are endpoints. The sole retained selection adjacent to  $w_j$  is  $(0,9+6j)$ , whose original occupied degree was zero and becomes one.No other retained selection gains an occupied neighbour. This proves feasibility for every  $S$ , including consecutive indices.3. The restricted budget and no-freezing lemmas are validWrite the endpoint set in the restricted class as
$$P=P_0\cup X\cup Y,
\qquad
Y\subseteq G(X).$$
This allows arbitrary rematching and arbitrary further withdrawal of original selections.The exact shield count and budgetEach entry has its own private row-1 shield. The only overlap is that  $d_j,e_j$ , when both present, share  $f_j$ . Shields belonging to different indices do not coincide. Hence
$$|G(X)|=|X|+h(X).$$
Every shield in  $G(X)$  must leave the selected set: it would otherwise have both its retained original occupied neighbour and an occupied entry as neighbours.The original endpoint set is colour-balanced. Every site of  $X$  is black and every site of  $Y$  is white. Since each matching edge joins opposite colours,
$$|Y|=|X|.$$
It follows that
$$|M|-|M_0|=|X|,
\qquad
|T|-|T_0|\le-|G(X)|,$$
and therefore
$$J-J_0\le |X|-|G(X)|=-h(X).$$
This reasoning does not assume that an entry is matched to a shield; it uses only the complete endpoint set and bipartite colour balance.The claimed equality example is also valid: pair each entry with its private shield, retain  $M_0$ , withdraw all of  $G(X)$ , and leave the common shields empty. No retained selection gains an occupied neighbour.The no-freezing proof correctly excludes the own mateA converted private shield has no selected neighbour and at most two occupied neighbours: its original black neighbour and its corresponding entry. Its actual mate must be one of them. That mate cannot support its first freezing, leaving at most one usable witness.Thus every converted private shield is permanently unfrozen, regardless of rematching.A converted common shield  $f_j$  at a singly occupied index has the same obstruction. Its only possible occupied neighbours are  $g_j$  and the one present entry; the outer site  $w_j$  is excluded by the restricted footprint.Let  $D$  count indices with both entries present. Complete freezing would therefore require
$$Y\subseteq\{f_j:d_j,e_j\in X\},$$
so
$$|Y|\le D\le \frac{|X|}{2}.$$
Together with  $|Y|=|X|$ , this is impossible when  $X\ne\varnothing$ .This is an all-length obstruction. It does not assume that a common shield at a double index actually can freeze; it only identifies the sole remaining possible locations for converted endpoints.4. \tag{11}$$
with the usual index restrictions.Use the original witnesses for the  $K$ 's and  $V_j$ . At an expanded index use
$$e_j:\ b'_j,U_{j+1},
\qquad
g_j:\ H_j,b_j.$$

\rho(K_{3j+3})=\tau_j-2.$$

Every comparison is strict, and no own-mate witness is used.This completes an all-length counterexample to the necessity of the particular  $CD$ -based replacement.The weaker necessity statement is correctIf all old  $M_0$  edges are retained, every new black endpoint must be matched to a new white shield. Each new white shield has no selected neighbour and only one neighbour outside the new black endpoint set:
$$a_j:\ C_j,\qquad
b'_j:\ A_{j+1},\qquad
f_j:\ g_j.$$
Before the first new white shield freezes, no new black endpoint is kept, because its mate is a still-unfrozen new white shield. A new white shield can therefore have at most one kept neighbour. No first such freezing can occur.This proves the necessary statement that retaining all old matching edges is impossible for complete freezing when  $S\ne\varnothing$ .A precise replacement for the disputed sentence is:The construction also uses the cross matching  $C_ja_j,D_jd_j$  displayed in (1). Retaining all original  $M_0$  edges traps the converted shield pool, so some original matching edge must be changed.That states exactly what the note establishes without asserting uniqueness of the displayed rematching.7. Accepted scopeFor fixed  $P_S$  and  $T\subseteq T_0$ , the upper bound in Section 7 is correct. Disjointness excludes all  $3s$  converted shields from  $T$ , while any matching with endpoint set  $P_S$  has  $|M_0|+3s$  edges. Hence
$$J\le |T_0|-3s+|M_0|+3s=J_0.$$
The original construction attains this bound with complete freezing. Different  $S$ 's give different endpoint footprints, so the claimed  $2^m$  lower bound on distinct configurations is also valid.After correcting the  $g_m$  definition and narrowing the specific-rematching necessity language, I would ACCEPT the note’s explicit all-length construction and restricted obstruction. The own-mate exclusion is already respected by every supplied rank row. The accepted result concerns the stated footprint, selection domain, freezing dynamics, and token identities; it supplies no global  $5/6$  improvement or unrestricted footprint optimum.
